country.paper_says: The study concerns community-based water supply in Salatiga, Indonesia.
country.where: p. 1, Abstract and Introduction: "In Salatiga Indonesia"

study_design.paper_says: Primary questionnaire, interview, and field-observation data and secondary organizational/administrative data were analyzed quantitatively using Rapfish/MDS and strategically using SWOT.
study_design.where: p. 3, Research Method: "Primary data consist of questionair survey, interview, and field observation"; "The analysis is performed using Rapfish method... and SWOT analysis"

population.paper_says: Four CBWS organizations in two kelurahan of Salatiga City were studied; Table 2 reports their user households.
population.where: p. 4, §4.1 and Table 2: "The research is performed to 4 (four) CBWS in two Kelurahan at Salatiga City"

sample_size.paper_says: The organizational sample was four CBWS. Table 2 also reports 168 returned questionnaires in total (60, 49, 20, and 39), whereas the extracted field was left blank.

urban_rural.paper_says: The study was conducted in Salatiga City and describes Rapfish as applicable to urban water and sanitation schemes, supporting an urban setting; the paper does not separately label it peri-urban.
urban_rural.where: pp. 1 and 4, Introduction and §4.1: "Salatiga City"; p. 6, ref. 6: "Urban Water and Sanitation Schemes"

service_provider.paper_says: The four providers studied were Tirta Barokah, Tirta Sejahtera, Tirta Kamandanu, and Tirto Agung.
service_provider.where: p. 4, Table 2, "List of Community Based Water Supply (CBWS) at Salatiga Studied"

regulatory_model.paper_says: CBWS systems are constructed by government but operated and managed by communities, including tariff setting. They complement limited PDAM coverage, and the study formulated Rapfish attributes using Permendagri and BPPSPAM criteria.
regulatory_model.where: p. 1, Introduction; p. 2, §2.1: "constructed by the government but its operation management including its agreed tariffs performed by a community"; p. 3, Research Method: "attributes... formulated by considering attributes on Permendagri and BPPSPAM"

effect_measure.paper_says: The study used Rapfish multi-dimensional scaling to score sustainability and Monte Carlo simulation to assess deviations, discrepancies, and scoring subjectivity.

effect_estimate.paper_says: All four CBWS were sustainable on ecological, technological, and social dimensions. Tirta Barokah and Tirta Sejahtera were institutionally and economically sustainable, whereas Tirta Kamandanu and Tirta Agung had low institutional scores of 30.82 and 38.64 and economic scores of 28.57 and 29.30. Monte Carlo discrepancies were below 1.5%. The conclusions identify management practices rather than source-water type as decisive and recommend institutional and economic improvements with outside-government facilitation.
effect_estimate.where: pp. 4–5, §4.2–4.3; p. 6, Conclusion and Recommendation, items 2–4

extraction_note.paper_says: The extraction note identifies the supplied paper record as R0EED09DB6147; this is review metadata rather than information reported in the article.
extraction_note.where: Review record metadata; not a paper field

parsed.overall_comment: The extraction is substantively supported, including the reported MDS findings and management-focused conclusions. The main discrepancy is the blank sample-size field: the paper explicitly studied four CBWS and reports 168 returned questionnaires.
